name: Lip plates

card.summary: Large discs worn in a stretched hole in the lip, a traditional adornment in parts of Africa and Amazonia that is also copied as extreme lip stretching.
card.note: Can affect teeth, gums and eating; stretching is permanent in effect.

quick.overview:
A lip plate is a disc, traditionally clay or wood, worn in a pierced and gradually stretched lip. Among the Mursi and Surma of Ethiopia, women are pierced as teenagers before marriage and increase plate size over time, and some Amazonian groups such as the Kayapo traditionally have men wear them. For wearers the plate is part of how they present themselves and mark life stages.

In looksmaxxing forums the topic appears as lip stretching and 'mouth widening appliances', where users ask whether stretching devices could change lip or mouth shape. Medical writing on labrets documents their effects on the jaw and teeth.
quick.how: Traditionally the lip is pierced and plates are changed to larger sizes gradually over a long period, with the wearer often making her own plate. Western body-modification fans stretch lip piercings to large gauges, and forum users discuss 3D-printed stretching appliances.
quick.risks: Reported risks include infection at piercing, difficulty eating and salivating, gum irritation and disease, and tooth gapping or erosion. The Ethiopian government has pressured communities to stop the practice. A medical review describes consequences for jaws and teeth.

lead: Lip plates, also called lip discs or plugs, are large discs, usually clay or wood, worn in a stretched hole in the lower or upper lip. Archaeological evidence suggests labrets were invented independently in Africa, Mesoamerica and coastal Ecuador. [1][2]

Groups that wear them include the Mursi and Surma of Ethiopia, where girls are pierced around ages 15 to 18 and plates can exceed 20 cm, the Sara and Lobi of Chad, the Makonde, and Amazonian groups such as the Kayapo. [1] Many writers claim plate size signals status or bride price, but this is not well sourced, and anthropologist David Turton disputed the bride-price link. [1]

A 2017 historical review of labrets in Africa and Amazonia covers their history, medical effects on jaws and teeth, and cultural determinants. [3] On looksmax.org, users discuss lip stretching appliances, including 3D-printed designs, for changing lip or mouth width. [4][5]

angle.text: Wearers deliberately reshape the lip so it holds a disc, a traditional mark of adult beauty and identity. Some forum users explore stretching devices to alter lip or mouth dimensions.

infobox: Mursi, Surma, Sara, Lobi, Makonde, Kayapo

paras: Mursi and Surma wearers typically make and decorate their own plates. [1] Pacific Northwest groups (Haida, Tsimshian, Tlingit) once used labrets to signal readiness for marriage; among the Aztecs they were linked to nobility and eloquence. [1][2] Some scholars connect the Ethiopian practice to female strength and self-esteem. [1]
In 1930 the Ringling Bros. circus displayed 13 Congolese people with lip plates as the 'Ubangi Savages', a name chosen from an African map for its exotic sound. [6]
Risks include infection at piercing, difficulty eating and salivating, gum disease and tooth gapping or erosion. [1][3] The Ethiopian government has pressured communities to stop. [1]
Looksmax.org threads share models for 3D-printed 'mouth widening appliances' and ask whether devices make the lip thinner or whether one is good. [4][5]
No studies found on lip stretching for cosmetic shaping. Related historical and medical literature on traditional labrets exists. [3]

timeline.event: Circus displays Congolese women as 'Ubangi Savages'. [6]

lore.intro: Forum threads treat lip stretching as an experimental route to changing mouth proportions. [4][5]

claims.claim: Stretching appliances can widen the mouth or thin the lip
claims.believers: Posters share 3D-printed appliances and ask if they thin the upper lip. [4][5]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested such appliances; literature documents jaw and teeth effects of labrets. [3]
